items.text: “Some of you got to it. Some didn’t. Both are fine.”
“Anyone want to say one sentence about how that landed for you?” — an arranged parent starts
Receive without commentary
“Good. Some of that work continues whether or not we got to it this week.”
The threefold cord is stronger because the strands hold each other in tension — the strength is in the holding
Four conditions have been quietly holding this room for four weeks. Tonight we name them
SAFE — the hearing condition. “I will not be judged as a person while I am doing my work” — Romans 14:3–4
PRESENT — the attention condition. “I am actually here” — aware that the Great I AM is also here — Revelation 1:8
CLEAR — the channel condition. Nothing unaddressed between God and me, or the circle and me — Matthew 7:5
INTENTIONAL — the obedience condition. On purpose, watching for what God is doing, willing to do it — John 5:19

panel.label: ECCLESIASTES 4:9–12
lines: “Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. … And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him—a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”

items.text: Each cluster takes the four conditions and asks: “for each one, where in my actual friendships does this show up? And where is it missing?”
“We are not naming names tonight. ‘One of my friends’ is fine.” — we map conditions, not people
Your Companion goes first on every condition, then one of the parents opens the round
Teens, you choose your own depth. Pass anytime
Twenty-eight minutes — same rooms as the last two weeks
Four conditions, about six minutes each — the Companion models first, the arranged parent opens the round
Each turn 30–60 seconds — specific: one friendship where the condition is present, one where it is missing
“No names of people who aren’t in this room — and for people who are, ‘one of my friendships’ or ‘one adult relationship in my life’ is the language. Nobody asks who you meant.”
Parents map their own adult friendships — not their teens’
If time remains, the quiet final question: “Of the four conditions, which one is the one I find hardest to offer to my friends?”
What happened in your cluster stays in your cluster
Patterns only — general, no names: “Many of us noticed Safety is the rarest condition in our friendships”
Each Cluster Companion takes ninety seconds — one or two general patterns from their circle
Then the Lead Companion names one observation across the clusters — “that is real, and it is the seed of the practice this week”

slides.title: Between-Session Practice — One Friendship, One Condition

items.text: “Pick one friendship in your life. Just one.” — you don’t have to tell anyone which one
Pick one of the four conditions — the one most missing there, or the one you find hardest to offer
Practice that one condition in that one friendship more intentionally than usual this week — practically
Presence — your phone is in another room. Clear — name something you have been quietly carrying
“One friendship. One condition. Practice. Journal what happens.” — Week 5 journal pages, card H5.5
The morning question and evening journal note continue daily
